segments.text: Kiva walked between Perrin and Anwen with her head up and her bound hand against her coat. She did not look at anybody. She felt them look at her, in green and in grey and in the colours of six circuits, under the white lamps that did not flicker. She felt it as a weight on the side of her face, and her neck, and the backs of her hands. It was not unkind. It was worse than unkind. It was the way people look at a thing that has been sent for.
